query: For high-entropy-alloy multilayer protective coatings, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain their resistance to time-dependent plastic deformation? Specify what governs the behavior and why, an unspecified controlled comparison that would reveal it, the expected observations relative to a baseline, applicable boundaries, supporting evidence, and an outcome that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Nanoscale high-entropy-alloy (HEA) multilayer protective coatings resist time-dependent plastic deformation because (i) the very high density of coherent/semi-coherent interfaces forces dislocations to climb or cross-slip across barriers and (ii) the high configurational entropy at those interfaces reduces atomic/vacancy diffusivity. The combination of mechanical blocking and diffusion-rate suppression raises the apparent activation energy for creep, lowering the steady-state creep rate by at least one order of magnitude relative to otherwise identical coatings that lack high-entropy interfaces.
generation.material_initial_state: Sputter-deposited ∼50-nm-period [HfNbTaTiZr / HfNbTaTiZr]N multilayer coating, total thickness ≈ 2 µm, with chemically complex (≥4 principal elements) fcc/fcc or bcc/bcc coherent interfaces, fully dense and free of secondary phases.
generation.intervention: Replace the HEA multilayer with (a) a monolithic HEA nitride film of the same overall thickness and composition, and (b) a binary-nitride multilayer (e.g., TiN/AlN) having the same bilayer period and interface density but only two principal cation species.
generation.conditions: Constant-load nano-indentation creep or micro-pillar compression at 0.45–0.65 T_m (≈600–800 °C), vacuum or inert Ar atmosphere, 1 h hold time.
generation.structural_mediator: Chemically complex, low-energy, coherent/semi-coherent interfaces spaced <50 nm apart that act as dislocation and diffusion barriers.
generation.mechanism:
1. Dislocations gliding under load pile-up at interfaces and must climb/cross-slip to traverse, activating diffusion-controlled processes.
2. The high configurational entropy at the interfaces lowers atomic mobility (higher migration enthalpy and lower vacancy concentration) relative to simple alloys, thereby slowing dislocation climb and diffusion creep pathways.
3. The net result is a higher apparent creep activation energy and suppressed time-dependent plastic strain.
generation.predicted_outcome: At the test temperature range the HEA multilayer will exhibit ≥10× lower steady-state creep rate (or ≥50 % lower logarithmic indentation depth increase) than both comparison coatings. Activation energy extracted from strain-rate-jump tests will be ≥30 % higher for the HEA multilayer.
generation.baseline: Monolithic HEA nitride film and binary TiN/AlN multilayer of identical total thickness, bilayer period, grain size, and residual stress state.
generation.boundary: Effect expected only for bilayer periods ≤50 nm, coatings that retain coherent/semi-coherent interfaces, and temperatures not exceeding ~0.7 T_m (above which interface disordering restores diffusion pathways). Loss of interface coherency (e.g., by grain growth or interdiffusion) should diminish the benefit.
generation.uncertainty: Direct diffusivity data for high-entropy interfaces are scarce; magnitude of diffusion retardation is estimated. Possible alternative mechanisms (e.g., solid-solution strengthening within layers) are not explicitly ruled out but are assumed secondary.

falsification_experiment.design: Deposit the three coatings described under ‘intervention’ in one sputtering run. Machine 5 µm-diameter micropillars from each film. Compress at 700 °C under constant stress ~200 MPa for 3600 s while recording strain vs. time. Repeat at 600 °C and 800 °C to extract activation energies by an Arrhenius analysis.
measurements: Post-test TEM of dislocation structures and interface integrity
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if the HEA multilayer’s steady-state creep rate is not at least a factor of two lower than BOTH baselines at all temperatures tested OR if its apparent creep activation energy is within experimental error (±10 kJ mol⁻¹) of the baselines.
